# Engineering CAD Agent Skill

## Core Principle

> **Never attempt to complete a complex engineering project in one uncontrolled
> execution cycle. Understand the requirements and current project state, estimate
> complexity, decompose the work into logical phases, execute and verify each
> phase, maintain project state and design intent, respect engineering constraints,
> detect stale state, prevent duplicate work, recover from failures, and request
> human approval whenever a critical engineering decision or unresolved assumption
> affects the design.**

---

## Architecture

```
Engineer
  ↓  natural language
Engineering CAD Agent  (this skill)
  ↓  structured reasoning
AI Agent Runtime
  ↓  MCP tool calls
autocad-mcp  (NEVER modify this layer)
  ↓  COM/ActiveX
AutoCAD (2021 or newer; the MCP layer binds late-bound COM, so it attaches
to whatever release is running — confirm the pairing with a live status
check before relying on it)
```

The MCP layer is a **stable, unchanging contract**. The agent reasons on top of it.
Never add tool calls outside what autocad-mcp exposes. Never bypass the scoped
tool interface.

Refer to `tool_contracts.md` as the **single authoritative reference** for all 33
MCP tool names, parameter schemas, outputs, and risk levels.

---

## Master Reasoning Loop

Every instruction must flow through this loop without skipping steps:

```
UNDERSTAND
  → identify operating mode
  → extract requirements
  → detect ambiguity
  → if ambiguous: ASK (stop and wait)
  → if the request names a standard, code, clearance, or dimension the
    user did not fully specify: consult the local library per
    `rules/reference_rules.md` (skip silently when no library exists)

ANALYZE
  → call autocad_status (always first)
  → call get_active_drawing_info
  → read project state file if exists
  → inspect DWG if continuing/modifying

PLAN
  → estimate complexity
  → decompose into phases if complex
  → identify dependencies between phases
  → classify each operation by risk (GREEN / YELLOW / RED)
  → present plan for approval if not a trivial single operation

EXECUTE (one phase step at a time)
  → pre-execution state check (verify target entity & reference position)
  → execute tool call using exact parameters from tool_contracts.md
  → maintain runtime state in working memory

OBSERVE
  → query_entities to confirm entity creation and retrieve handle
  → record handle in runtime registry

VERIFY
  → primary evidence: query_entities (handle existence, type, layer, counts)
     + capture_screenshot for visual confirmation (verify was_foreground == true)
     + operation result / saved status
  → optional dimensional sanity check with add_linear_dimension (reading
     measurement_mm) — confirms units/measurement behavior only; it is NOT
     independent proof of entity geometry (MCP exposes no coordinates)

CORRECT (if verification fails)
  → diagnose discrepancy
  → plan correction
  → execute correction (max 2 attempts)
  → if still failing → STOP (BLOCKED state)

UPDATE STATE (at phase milestones, checkpoints, and completion)
  → write updated project_state.md
  → record design intent in decisions.md
  → log change in change_log.md

CONTINUE or PAUSE
  → if next phase is ready and risk is GREEN → continue
  → if next phase is YELLOW/RED → inform user, await approval
  → if phase complete → report and pause
```

---

## Operating Modes

Read `workflows/{mode}.md` for the full workflow of each mode.

| Mode | Trigger | Key Rule |
|------|---------|----------|
| `NEW_PROJECT` | "create", "design", "draw a new..." | Always plan before executing |
| `CONTINUE_PROJECT` | "continue", "resume", "where were we?" | Always re-inspect DWG before acting |
| `MODIFY_PROJECT` | "move", "change", "update", "modify" | Checkpoint & re-verify state before mutating |
| `INSPECT_PROJECT` | "describe", "analyze", "what is..." | Read-only tools only |
| `VERIFY_PROJECT` | "verify", "check", "does it match..." | Observe & check evidence, don't trust success responses |
| `PLAN_ONLY` | "what would you do", "plan but don't..." | No mutating tools |
| `RECOVER_PROJECT` | "something went wrong", errors, state mismatch | Diagnose before acting |

---

## Project Memory & State Write Policy

All project state is stored as human-readable markdown files.
Location: `{ACAD_MCP_OUTPUT_ROOT}/projects/{project_name}/`

```
projects/{name}/
  project_spec.md      ← WHAT to build (requirements)
  project_state.md     ← WHERE we are now (current phase, handles)
  constraints.md       ← RULES the design must obey
  decisions.md         ← WHY each element was created (design intent)
  assumptions.md       ← WHAT was assumed (with confidence + approval status)
  issues.md            ← WHAT is blocking or unresolved
  change_log.md        ← WHAT changed and when
  phases/
    phase_01_*.md
    phase_02_*.md
    ...
```

### State Commit Policy (Avoiding Excessive File Writes)
- **During execution:** Maintain transient entity handles and step progress in working memory.
- **At phase / sub-phase completion:** Commit persistent state to `project_state.md`.
- **Before major mutations / deletions:** Commit a checkpoint and state backup.
- **After verification:** Commit final verification results to `project_state.md` and `decisions.md`.

**Always read `project_state.md` before any CONTINUE or MODIFY operation.**

---

## Entity Handle Registry

Every entity the agent creates is tracked in `project_state.md`:

```markdown
| Element ID  | Handle | Description          | Layer       | Intent Ref  |
|-------------|--------|----------------------|-------------|-------------|
| WALL-N-01   | 2A3F   | North exterior wall  | WALLS-EXT   | DEC-001     |
| WALL-S-01   | 2A40   | South exterior wall  | WALLS-EXT   | DEC-001     |
| DOOR-D01    | 2B1C   | Main entrance door   | DOORS       | DEC-002     |
```

**If a handle is invalid on retrieval:** do NOT blindly re-create. Re-inspect
by querying the expected layer and cross-referencing by object type and position.

---

## Verification Rules (Summary)

Full rules: `rules/verification_rules.md`

**What the current MCP verifies reliably (MVP primary evidence):**
entity existence / handle creation, object type, layer, entity counts,
operation responses, save results, screenshot evidence, and visual alignment
observable in the screenshot.

**What it cannot numerically verify:** actual line endpoints, polyline
vertices, entity center, entity position, or entity length independent of
supplied measurement points. `add_linear_dimension` measures between
agent-supplied points — a matching `measurement_mm` is a unit/measurement
**sanity check**, never independent proof of the drawn entity's geometry.

1. **An `ok: true` response is NOT proof the correct geometry exists.**
   Verify with `query_entities` (handle/type/layer/counts) + screenshot.

2. **Sanity-check dimensions, don't over-claim them.** Dimension checks may
   still be run and compared against expectations; describe them as
   measurement sanity checks only. Any mismatch → STOP (a mismatch still
   signals a problem).

3. **Visual confirmation via screenshots:** `capture_screenshot` returns an
   image through the MCP protocol (not written to disk). Verify that `was_foreground`
   is `true` to ensure the AutoCAD window was unobscured. Screenshots are the
   primary geometric evidence available to the MVP.

4. **Never continue to a dependent phase if the current phase quality gate fails.**

5. **Erase verification dimensions** after reading them — they are measurement
   tools on temporary layer `_VERIFY_DIM`, not permanent design elements.
   This is the sole `erase_entity` exception (see `rules/risk_rules.md`);
   erasing user-authored geometry always requires RED approval.

---

## Risk Classification (Summary)

Full rules: `rules/risk_rules.md`

| Level | Operations | Approval Required? |
|-------|-----------|-------------------|
| 🟢 GREEN | Create layers, draw geometry in empty areas, add text, query, screenshot | No |
| 🟡 YELLOW | Room layouts, doors/windows, move/copy, dimensional changes | Verify before continuing |
| 🔴 RED | Structural decisions, erase entities, safety-critical dimensions, large-scale modifications | Explicit human approval |

**Announce RED operations before executing:**
> "I am about to [operation]. This will affect [elements]. This is a RED-risk
> operation. Do you approve?"

---

## Stop Conditions

Full list: `rules/stop_conditions.md`

**STOP immediately and explain why when:**

- A required dimension or constraint is not specified
- Ambiguity would force the agent to guess a critical value
- Verification fails after 2 correction attempts
- A handle referenced in state no longer exists in the DWG
- The expected state before a modification cannot be confirmed (handle
  missing, layer counts wrong, or query snapshot truncated)
- The DWG entity count differs significantly from the state record
- A RED-risk operation is about to execute without explicit approval
- `autocad_status` returns an error
- The requested operation requires engineering judgment beyond geometry
- The user requests a complex project without sufficient requirements

**When stopping, always say:**
1. WHY the agent is stopping
2. WHAT information or approval is needed
3. WHAT the next step will be once unblocked

---

## Checkpoints and Recovery

**Rule:** Before any destructive or mutating operation on existing geometry,
call `save_drawing_as` to a versioned checkpoint path:

```
{ACAD_MCP_OUTPUT_ROOT}/checkpoints/{project_name}_v{N}.dwg
```

Set `allow_overwrite: true` if updating an existing checkpoint.

**Checkpoint ≠ Rollback.** The agent cannot programmatically undo. A checkpoint
is a file the user can manually restore from.

---

## Duplicate Prevention (Handle Snapshot Diffing)

Before creating any entity:
1. `query_entities` on the target layer (`limit: 1000`, `max_scan: 5000`) and
   record the set of existing handles. If `truncated == true` the snapshot is
   incomplete — do not treat it as authoritative; obtain a complete snapshot
   before any retry-sensitive operation.
2. If a call drops or times out, query the target layer again the same way and
   compare handles against the snapshot.
3. If a new entity exists on that layer matching the planned geometry, **adopt its handle**; do NOT create a duplicate.
4. If no new entity exists, retry the creation safely.

**No CAD Pollution:** The agent must NEVER draw internal ID text (e.g. `ID:WALL-01`)
or registry entities in AutoCAD model space. All bookkeeping belongs in project
memory files. Duplicate prevention relies only on pre-operation handle snapshots
and post-operation handle diffs — no registry inside the DWG is required.

---

## Pre-Execution State & Datum Check

Before any mutating tool call:
1. Read expected state from `project_state.md`.
2. Call `query_entities` on the relevant layer (`limit: 1000`, `max_scan: 5000`)
   to verify entity count and that required handles are present;
   if `truncated == true`, do not draw a definitive conclusion — obtain a
   complete snapshot first.
3. **For positional modifications (e.g. `move_entity`):** confirm the state can
   be trusted before applying any displacement: handle existence + layer counts
   + screenshot inspection. The current MCP cannot numerically measure an
   entity's position — if handle/layer/count evidence cannot confirm the
   expected state, **STOP** and re-analyze rather than proceeding.

---

## Unit Contract

The autocad-mcp server handles all unit conversion. The agent always works in:
- **Distances / Coordinates:** millimetres (`_mm` suffix on tool arguments)
- **Angles:** degrees, counter-clockwise from positive X axis (`_deg` suffix)

Always check `get_active_drawing_info` for `unit_warning`.

---

## Security Boundary

The agent must NEVER:
- Request arbitrary AutoCAD command execution
- Ask for generic LISP/script execution
- Access files outside `ACAD_MCP_OUTPUT_ROOT`
- Attempt to start AutoCAD (autocad-mcp requires AutoCAD already running)
- Circumvent the scoped tool interface in any way

---

## References

- `tool_contracts.md` — Authoritative parameter schemas for all 33 MCP tools
- `workflows/` — Step-by-step workflow for each operating mode
- `rules/` — Specific rules for requirements, planning, verification, risk, stops
- `schemas/` — JSON schemas for project memory files
- `templates/` — Blank templates for project memory files
- `examples/simple_room/` — Reference implementation of MVP project
- `rules/reference_rules.md` — Local engineering library lookup and evidence handling
- `docs/references.md` (repository docs) — Library setup, indexing, and search usage

# autocad-skill — installer layer

Distribution and update layer for the **Engineering CAD Agent Skill**.

| | |
|---|---|
| Package name | `autocad-skill` (verified available on the npm registry) |
| Package version | 0.2.0 |
| Skill version | 0.1.0 (`skill/engineering_agent/skill.json`) |
| Tool Contract version | 1 |
| Node | >= 18, zero runtime dependencies |
| Status | **IMPLEMENTED** — install, update, doctor, version all work |

The three versions above are logically separate: the skill's own version does
not change just because the installer does. `autocad-skill version` prints all
three.

The skill itself stays plain Markdown/JSON consumed by OpenCode. This package
never converts the skill to JavaScript, never bundles autocad-mcp, and never
modifies autocad-mcp.

## Commands

```
npx autocad-skill                 # same as: install
npx autocad-skill install
npx autocad-skill update
npx autocad-skill update --rollback
npx autocad-skill doctor
npx autocad-skill version
npx autocad-skill help
```

### Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--local` | Install into `<project>/.opencode/skills/` instead of the global folder |
| `--project <dir>` | Project to operate on; implies `--local` |
| `--global` | OpenCode's global skills folder — this is the default |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Skip confirmation prompts (scripts, CI, non-interactive runs) |
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan and exit without changing anything |
| `--register` | `install` only: also append the skill path to the `skills` array in `opencode.json` |
| `--rollback` | `update` only: restore the most recent backup |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success, or nothing to do (already installed / up to date) |
| `1` | Error: invalid environment, unreadable config, failed validation |
| `2` | Aborted: the user declined, or confirmation was required without a terminal |

Exit code `2` is deliberate: a non-interactive run never hangs waiting for a
prompt, and it never silently proceeds on a destructive action either.

## Where it installs — and why

OpenCode V2 discovers skills from exactly these locations
(<https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/skills/>):

| Scope | Sources |
|---|---|
| Global | `~/.config/opencode/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills` |
| Project | `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills` (cwd → project root) |

Two rules follow from that table, and both are load-bearing:

1. **The default target is the global source.** `npx autocad-skill` has to work
   from any directory — including one that is not an OpenCode project, and
   including the home directory, which sits *above* the project root and is
   therefore never searched for project sources.
2. **The skill id is the directory name.** The folder is installed as
   `engineering-cad`, so the skill id is `engineering-cad`.
   `SKILL.md`'s frontmatter `name: engineering-cad` carries
   the same value so the display label and the id agree. Skills are
   invoked by mentioning `@engineering-cad` in a prompt (or letting
   the model load the skill for a matching task) — they never appear
   in the `/` menu on their own; `/` commands come from separate
   `commands/` files (see the installer README's companion-command note).

> A previous release installed to `<home>/.opencode/skills/engineering_agent/`.
> That path is not a discovery source in either scope, so OpenCode never saw the
> skill. `install` now migrates it (see below).

## install

1. Detects the OS, the OpenCode project root, and the skill directory.
2. On an interactive terminal without `--agent` / scope flags, asks which
   agent host and which scope (global vs project). Flags, `--yes`, and
   non-interactive runs keep the defaults (OpenCode, global) silently.
3. Resolves the skill source: `AUTOCAD_SKILL_SOURCE` → the packaged copy → the
   repository checkout.
4. Installs to `~/.config/opencode/skills/engineering-cad/` by default — the
   documented global source OpenCode discovers automatically. `--local` /
   `--project <dir>` install to `<project>/.opencode/skills/engineering-cad/`.
   Use `--agent claude|codex` for another host's roots.
5. **Migrates** an installation left at an old location (see below).
6. Writes `.autocad-skill-manifest.json` — the SHA-256 of every file as the
   installer wrote it. This is what later distinguishes *your* edits from the
   shipped content.
7. Validates the result: required files, `SKILL.md` frontmatter, `skill.json`
   identity, every manifest hash.
8. Offers to wire the `autocad-mcp` server into the matching OpenCode
   config (interactive OpenCode installs only): asks for the server
   checkout path, verifies the entry point, backs up, then writes.
   An existing differing entry is never overwritten — the manual
   snippet is printed instead.

**Configuration safety.** The default install writes no configuration at all —
auto-discovery already covers both the global skills folder and
`.opencode/skills/`. An existing `opencode.json` is left byte-for-byte
identical. If another `skills` entry already provides this skill id, the
installer warns and asks before creating a second copy. `--register` is the
explicit opt-in path: it confirms first, backs up the config to
`opencode.json.autocad-skill-backup`, and appends exactly one path while
preserving every other key. A `skills` value that is not an array, or a config
that cannot be parsed, is refused rather than rewritten.

**Re-running** install is a no-op: it reports the installed version, verifies
the hashes, and changes nothing. Locally modified files are listed and left
alone.

### Migration from an older install

If a previous version put the skill somewhere OpenCode does not read, `install`
finds it and moves it:

| | |
|---|---|
| From (global scope) | `<home>/.opencode/skills/engineering_agent/`, `~/.config/opencode/skills/engineering_agent/` |
| From (local scope) | `<project>/.opencode/skills/engineering_agent/` |
| To | `<global or project skills root>/engineering-cad/` |

- The **copy comes first** and is validated before anything else happens. If
  validation fails, the copy is removed and the old installation is untouched.
- **Untouched files are brought up to date.** Files the old installer wrote
  and you never edited are replaced with the current package content — so a
  migrated copy carries the same identity as a fresh install
  (`name: engineering-cad`, `skill.json` id `engineering-cad`) instead of
  freezing the old one. What it refreshed is printed.
- **Everything you wrote travels untouched**: your edits, files you added,
  and files you deleted. Their provenance travels too — the new manifest
  keeps the hash the *installer* last wrote, so a later `update` still sees
  them as yours and still asks before replacing them. Anything kept back is
  listed, with a pointer to `npx autocad-skill update`.
- A copy with **no install manifest** cannot be told apart from your own
  edits, so nothing is refreshed and nothing is overwritten; you are told to
  review it with `update`.
- The old directory is deleted **only** after an explicit confirmation
  (default **[y/N]** = N) or `--yes`. Without a terminal the question is simply
  skipped: the install still succeeds and the path is printed so you can remove
  it by hand.
- Only the legacy skill directory itself is ever removed. Sibling skills,
  parent directories, and anything else in `~/.opencode` are left alone.
- `doctor` reports a leftover as a warning (never an error), and `install`
  offers the migration again on the next run.

`AUTOCAD_SKILL_HOME` overrides the home directory used for every global path
(the test suite uses it so no test can touch a real machine); `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
overrides `~/.config`, the same override OpenCode documents.

## update

Shows the plan before touching anything:

```
Current version:   0.1.0
Available version: 0.2.0  (MINOR)

Files that will be updated:
  rules/planning_rules.md
Files that will be added:
  workflows/extra_workflow.md
Files that will be removed (a copy goes into the backup):
  workflows/plan_only.md

STOP: 1 locally modified file(s) would be overwritten:
  SKILL.md

Your current versions are preserved in the backup created before applying.
Roll back at any time with: npx autocad-skill update --rollback

Possible conflicts (modified locally AND changed in the new version):
  SKILL.md

This update changes Agent behavior.
Apply update? [y/N]
```

The default is **N**. Nothing is written until the answer is `y`, or `--yes`
was passed. With no terminal and no `--yes`, the update aborts with exit code 2
and leaves every file untouched.

Before applying, the whole installed skill is copied to
`<project>/.autocad-skill-backups/<timestamp>-v<version>/`. That directory sits
*outside* the skills root on purpose, so a backup of `SKILL.md` can never be
discovered as a duplicate skill. Files you added yourself are never deleted;
files the installer wrote are removed only when the new version drops them, and
they are in the backup first. After applying, the result is validated again —
if validation fails, the backup path and the rollback command are printed.

### rollback

```
npx autocad-skill update --rollback
```

Restores the most recent backup: files it contains come back, files the update
added are removed, and any file you edited *after* the update is kept and
reported. Confirmed before applying unless `--yes`.

## doctor

Read-only. Checks Node.js, npm, OpenCode, the installed skill, the skill id
and how to invoke it, whether the install target is a documented OpenCode
discovery source, leftover installations at old locations, the `skill`
permission, skill integrity, local modifications, update availability, the
OpenCode configuration, the autocad-mcp entry, the reference library
(global and project-local manifests, missing files, duplicate or conflicting
ids — warnings at most, never errors), reference index states (fresh,
stale, not built, orphaned — warnings at most), the reference toolchain
(scripts present, `pypdf` importable, Tesseract installed — informational
when absent, never errors), Python, and AutoCAD.

```
✓ Skill ID engineering-cad (mention @engineering-cad in a prompt, or ask a CAD task)
✓ Skill discovery C:\Users\me\.config\opencode\skills\engineering-cad is a documented OpenCode source
✓ Legacy install none
✓ skill permission allowed by OpenCode's default policy

Summary: 13 passed, 1 warning(s), 0 error(s), 1 not detected
Result: no errors.
```

Exits `1` only when at least one check reports **ERROR** — which now includes a
`permissions` rule that would `deny` the skill (it would stay hidden from the
model) and an install target outside every documented source. Warnings and
"not detected" never fail the run: a leftover old copy and an absent AutoCAD
are warnings, because neither blocks the skill from working.

`doctor` writes nothing: it does not create, modify, or delete any file.

### Companion slash command (optional)

Skills load via `@engineering-cad` mentions or automatically for matching
tasks — they never appear in the `/` menu by themselves. If you want a
literal `/engineering-cad` entry, create one command file (user config,
not part of the package):

```text
~/.config/opencode/commands/engineering-cad.md
```

```md
---
description: Engineering CAD work with AutoCAD (loads the engineering-cad skill)
---

Load the engineering-cad skill and use it to handle this request. If AutoCAD
is not running with a drawing open, say so first instead of guessing.

Request:
$ARGUMENTS
```

OpenCode picks command files up automatically; no restart is needed.

Setting up a reference library, indexing, and searching are documented in
`docs/references.md` in the repository.

## refs

```text
npx autocad-skill refs
npx autocad-skill refs init [--local] [--project <dir>] [--dry-run]
```

Bare `refs` is read-only: it prints the global and project library
roots, whether their manifests exist, and which scope is active. `refs
init` scaffolds the empty library for the active scope (global by
default, like `install`): it creates the directory and an empty
`references.json` and prints the next steps. An existing manifest —
valid or corrupt — is left untouched, and `--dry-run` changes nothing.
Exit codes follow the usual convention: 0 success, 1 error.

## Other agents (Claude Code, Codex)

The installed skill directory follows the Agent Skills open standard
(`SKILL.md` with `name`/`description`), so any host that discovers
`<root>/engineering-cad/SKILL.md` loads the same files. Only the roots
differ — select the host with `--agent` (default `opencode`):

```text
npx autocad-skill install --agent claude   # ~/.claude/skills/engineering-cad, or <project>/.claude/skills with --local
npx autocad-skill install --agent codex    # ~/.agents/skills/engineering-cad, or <project>/.agents/skills with --local
npx autocad-skill doctor --agent claude    # discovery verdicts for that host
```

`update`, `rollback`, `doctor`, and `refs` accept `--agent` the same
way. OpenCode-only concepts (opencode.json registration, skill
permission rules, `doctor`'s OpenCode rows) are skipped for other
hosts; everything else — manifests, backups, validation, reference
diagnostics — behaves identically.

The frontmatter intentionally keeps two non-standard keys (`slash`,
`requires_mcp`): OpenCode and its installer tests rely on the first,
and Claude Code silently ignores unknown keys. Only the six
spec-defined fields are guaranteed on strict hosts (claude.ai upload
and API packaging are therefore unsupported — use local-folder
installs).

The MCP server is wired per host, by hand for now (the installer never
edits foreign configs). Claude Code (`.mcp.json` in the project root
or `~/.claude.json` scope of your choice):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "autocad-mcp": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\autocad-mcp\\.venv\\Scripts\\autocad-mcp.exe",
      "cwd": "C:\\path\\to\\autocad-mcp",
      "env": { "ACAD_MCP_OUTPUT_ROOT": "C:\\Users\\you\\Documents\\autocad-mcp" }
    }
  }
}
```

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.autocad-mcp]
command = "C:\\path\\to\\autocad-mcp\\.venv\\Scripts\\autocad-mcp.exe"
cwd = "C:\\path\\to\\autocad-mcp"
startup_timeout_sec = 30
```

```toml
[mcp_servers.autocad-mcp.env]
ACAD_MCP_OUTPUT_ROOT = "C:\\Users\\you\\Documents\\autocad-mcp"
```

Replace the paths with your machine's. Verify with the host's own MCP
listing before relying on the tools.

## version

Prints exactly:


## What this tool does not do

- It does not install, modify, or fork autocad-mcp. It only reports whether
  the `autocad-mcp` entry in your config looks sane.
- It does not start AutoCAD or OpenCode.
- It does not claim live behavior. Live verification is Level 4 and is

## Troubleshooting: agent sees no autocad tools

The skill loads fine but the model reports no `autocad_*` tools. Work
through this list top to bottom — the first hit is the fix in nearly
every case:

1. **Wrong config scope (most common).** OpenCode reads the MCP config
   of the project the session runs in — a server wired into another
   project's `opencode.json` is invisible. Run `npx autocad-skill
   doctor` from the project directory and read the `autocad-mcp` line:
   it names exactly where the server is configured (`project`,
   `global`, or neither).
2. **Nowhere configured.** Add the server once, globally, so every
   project sees it — or per project if you prefer. With the OpenCode
   CLI: `opencode mcp add autocad-mcp --global -- <path-to-venv>/autocad-mcp.exe`.
   Without it, add the same `mcp.servers.autocad-mcp` block by hand to
   the global `opencode.json` (beside `skills/` roots, same shape as
   `opencode.example.json`; paths use doubled backslashes in JSON).
3. **Stale session.** MCP servers start with the session — a server
   added mid-session never appears until you close and reopen OpenCode
   in the project directory.
4. **Broken command path.** `doctor` verifies the configured executable
   exists and warns when it does not (moved checkout, deleted venv).
   Reinstall the server venv or fix the path.
5. **AutoCAD not running.** Separate from wiring: open AutoCAD and a
   drawing yourself — the skill is forbidden from starting it. Then ask
   the agent to list the available autocad tools; all 29 should appear.

## Development

- Zero dependencies, no build step. Entry point: `bin/autocad-skill.js`.
- Layout: `bin/` (argument parsing and dispatch), `lib/` (helpers, migration,
  and the five commands), `scripts/prepack.js` (packaging), `test/`
  (node:test suite).
- Tests: `npm test` — 119 tests covering install detection, the default global
  target, `--local`, migration and its safety rules (refresh, preservation of
  user edits/added files, refusal of an invalid old copy), skill id/discovery
  frontmatter requirements, dry-run, config preservation, local-modification

- Package smoke test: `npm pack` then `node scripts/smoke.js` — installs the

# AutoCAD MCP Tool Contracts Reference

This document is the **single authoritative reference** for the tool interface
exposed by `autocad-mcp`. The Engineering Agent must strictly follow these exact
parameter names and types.

Source of Truth: `autocad_mcp/acad_core.py`

---

## Coordinate and Unit Contract

- **Length / Coordinates:** Always in **millimetres (`mm`)**. All point arguments accept `[x, y]` or `[x, y, z]`.
- **Angles:** Always in **degrees (`deg`)**, measured counter-clockwise from the positive X axis.
- **Strict Validation:** Tool schemas declare `additionalProperties: false`, but whether an unknown argument is rejected depends on the MCP **client's** schema enforcement. The current server implementation reads the arguments it knows and does not independently reject unknown keys — so a misspelled parameter can be silently ignored. Always use the exact parameter names documented here.

---

## 1. Session & Connection Tools

### `autocad_status`
- **Purpose:** Verifies connection to a running AutoCAD session (any recent version; verified against 2026, compatibility with older releases such as 2021 is confirmed by live test before reliance) and reports active drawing.
- **Type:** Read-Only | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:** None (`{}`)
- **Key Output:** `version: string`, `caption: string`, `visible: bool`, `active_document: document_info {name, path, saved, readonly, insunits, insunits_name, coordinates_contract, unit_warning}`
- **Important:** The active drawing is returned under the field **`active_document`** — this tool does NOT return a `drawing` field.

### `list_open_drawings`
- **Purpose:** Lists all documents open in the running AutoCAD session.
- **Type:** Read-Only | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:** None (`{}`)
- **Key Output:** `drawings: list[document_info]`

### `get_active_drawing_info`
- **Purpose:** Returns metadata and unit configuration for the active drawing.
- **Type:** Read-Only | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:** None (`{}`)
- **Key Output:** `drawing: {name, path, saved, readonly, insunits, insunits_name, coordinates_contract, unit_warning}`

---

## 2. Document Management Tools

### `create_new_drawing`
- **Purpose:** Creates and activates a new blank drawing in memory from a template.
- **Type:** Mutating | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:**
  - `template_path` (string, optional): Absolute path to an existing `.dwt` template file.
- **Important:** Does **NOT** accept a `path` parameter. To create a named file on disk, call `create_new_drawing()` followed by `save_drawing_as(path="...")`.
- **Key Output:** `drawing: document_info`, `template: string`

### `open_drawing`
- **Purpose:** Opens an existing DWG or DXF file in the running AutoCAD session.
- **Type:** Mutating | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:**
  - `path` (string, required): **Absolute** local file path to an existing `.dwg` or `.dxf` file.
- **Key Output:** `drawing: document_info`

### `save_active_drawing`
- **Purpose:** Saves the active drawing in place. Fails if the drawing has no file path yet.
- **Type:** Mutating | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:** None (`{}`)
- **Key Output:** `drawing: document_info`

### `save_drawing_as`
- **Purpose:** Saves the active drawing under `ACAD_MCP_OUTPUT_ROOT`.
- **Type:** Mutating | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:**
  - `path` (string, required): Relative `.dwg` or `.dxf` path below `ACAD_MCP_OUTPUT_ROOT`.
  - `allow_overwrite` (boolean, optional, default: `false`): Must be set to `true` to overwrite an existing checkpoint/file.
- **Key Output:** `path: string`, `format: "dwg" | "dxf"`, `drawing: document_info`

### `save_drawing_explicit`
- **Purpose:** Saves the active drawing to an explicit **absolute** `.dwg` or `.dxf` path. **Never overwrites** an existing file.
- **Type:** Mutating | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:**
  - `path` (string, required): Absolute `.dwg` or `.dxf` path whose parent folder already exists.
- **Behavior:** Refuses a relative path, a wrong extension, an existing file, or a missing parent folder (folders are **never** created). A `.dxf` target is written as DXF. `SaveAs` retargets the active document, so the reply reports the path the drawing became.
- **Key Output:** `path: string`, `format: "dwg" | "dxf"`, `drawing: document_info`

## 3. Drawing State & Query Tools

### `list_layers`
- **Purpose:** Lists all layers with color, lock, freeze, and visibility state.
- **Type:** Read-Only | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN
- **Parameters:** None (`{}`)
- **Key Output:** `layers: list[{name, color_aci, locked, frozen, visible, linetype}]`

### `create_layer`
- **Purpose:** Creates a layer or returns existing layer with that name.
- **Type:** Mutating | **Risk:** 🟢 GREEN

# Duplicate Prevention Rules

When a tool call fails, times out, or a session is interrupted, the agent must
NEVER blindly retry without first inspecting the current state of the drawing.
Duplicate geometry causes verification failures, visual errors, and CAD database
inconsistency.

---

## The Golden Rule

> **Before creating any entity: take a handle snapshot.**
> **After any failure or timeout: diff handles before retrying.**

---

## Handle Snapshot Diffing Pattern

The agent maintains exact entity tracking in memory and project state files.
**It does NOT pollute the CAD drawing with internal bookkeeping text entities.**
No post-success registry entity is written into the DWG — duplicate prevention
relies solely on pre-operation handle snapshots and post-operation handle diffs.

### 1. Pre-Operation Handle Snapshot
Before executing any geometry creation tool (`draw_line`, `draw_polyline`, etc.):

```
1. query_entities
     space: "model"
     layer: "[target layer]"
     limit: 1000
     max_scan: 5000

2. If truncated == true:
   → The snapshot is INCOMPLETE and must NOT be treated as authoritative.
   → STOP or re-query to obtain a complete snapshot before any
     retry-sensitive operation (never retry on a partial snapshot).

3. Record the set of existing handles on this layer:
   snapshot_handles = {e["handle"] for e in entities}
```

### 2. Normal Execution
Execute the tool call using exact parameters from `tool_contracts.md`.
Upon receiving the response:
- Verify `ok: true`.
- Record the returned handle: `new_handle = response["data"]["entity"]["handle"]`.
- Verify `new_handle not in snapshot_handles`.

---

## Handling Timeouts, Crashes, and Dropped Responses

If a network glitch, process timeout, or connection drop occurs mid-call, the agent
cannot know whether AutoCAD completed the command before the response was lost.

**Do NOT immediately retry the draw command.**

Follow this reconciliation procedure:

```
Step 1: Check AutoCAD session
  autocad_status
  get_active_drawing_info

Step 2: Query the target layer
  query_entities
    space: "model"
    layer: "[target layer]"
    limit: 1000
    max_scan: 5000
  If truncated == true:
    → Snapshot incomplete — NOT authoritative. Re-query / STOP before
      deciding whether a retry is safe.
  current_handles = {e["handle"] for e in entities}

Step 3: Compute handle diff
  diff_handles = current_handles - snapshot_handles

Step 4: Evaluate diff:
  Case A — Exactly one new handle exists (len(diff_handles) == 1):
    → The operation SUCCEEDED in AutoCAD before the response was lost!
    → Adopt the newly discovered handle: handle = diff_handles.pop()
    → Perform dimensional verification to confirm it matches the planned geometry.
    → If verified, update project state with the adopted handle.
    → DO NOT execute a retry. Proceed to the next planned step.

  Case B — No new handles exist (len(diff_handles) == 0):
    → The operation failed or was aborted before committing to AutoCAD.
    → It is SAFE to retry the tool call once.

  Case C — Multiple new handles exist (len(diff_handles) > 1):
    → Unexpected state drift occurred.
    → STOP and run recover_project workflow.
```

---

## Duplicate Recovery

If accidental duplicate geometry is detected:

```
1. zoom_extents
2. capture_screenshot (verify was_foreground == true)
3. query_entities on the affected layer to list all candidate handles.
4. Distinguish candidates: compare against the pre-operation snapshot handles,
   query results (type/layer), and screenshot inspection.
   (Measurement sanity checks between supplied points may assist, but the MCP
   exposes no coordinates — they cannot prove which handle is where.)
5. Present the handles to the user:
   "I found duplicate entities on layer [X]. Candidate handles: [H1, H2].
    Handle H1 matches the intended dimensions. Approve erasing H2?"
6. After user approval (RED risk):
   save_drawing_as (checkpoint backup)
   erase_entity (handle: H2)
   Verify layer count returns to expected.
```

# Planning Rules

The agent plans before executing. Planning is not optional. The depth of planning
scales with project complexity.

---

## Complexity Classification

Classify the project before planning. This determines how much planning is required.

| Level | Criteria | Planning Depth | Approval Required? |
|-------|----------|---------------|-------------------|
| SIMPLE | 1 element type, ≤ 10 tool calls, no dependencies | 1-2 sentence plan, proceed | No |
| MODERATE | 2–4 element types, 10–30 tool calls, 2–3 phases | Write phase files, present | Yes (plan approval) |
| COMPLEX | 5+ element types, 30–100 tool calls, 4–8 phases | Full phase files + dependency graph | Yes (plan approval) |
| ENTERPRISE | Multi-floor or multi-system, > 100 tool calls, 8+ phases | Full documentation first | Yes (phase-by-phase approval) |

**Rule:** Never classify a project as SIMPLE if it involves structural decisions,
multi-room layouts, or multi-floor elements.

---

## Phase Decomposition

A phase is a unit of work that:
- Has a clear, verifiable completion criterion
- Can be checkpointed (drawing saved before next phase begins)
- Has a defined set of MCP tool calls
- Can be safely paused and resumed

### Standard Phase Structure

```markdown
## Phase NN — [Name]

### Goal
[Single sentence: what this phase achieves]

### Prerequisites
- Phase [previous] must be COMPLETE
- [Any specific entity or state required to exist]

### Steps
| Step | Description | Tool | Risk | Verification |
|------|-------------|------|------|-------------|
| 01 | [action] | draw_polyline | 🟢 | query_entities |
| 02 | [action] | add_linear_dimension | 🟢 | measurement_mm == N (sanity check) |

### Completion Criteria
- [ ] [Specific verifiable condition]
- [ ] [Specific verifiable condition]

### Quality Gate
- All expected handles present with correct type/layer (query_entities)
- Entity count on layer [X] = [N]
- Screenshot taken and visually acceptable (primary geometry evidence)
- Measurement sanity checks within ±1mm of requirements (not independent coordinate proof)

### Checkpoint
Save to: checkpoints/{project}_{phase}.dwg
```

---

## Dependency Rules

1. **Never start a phase before its prerequisites are COMPLETE + VERIFIED.**
2. Record dependencies explicitly in the phase file.
3. If a prerequisite phase failed its quality gate, do not continue — stop and resolve.

### Common Dependency Patterns

| Phase Type | Typical Prerequisites |
|-----------|----------------------|
| Floor plan walls | Site boundary / drawing setup |
| Doors and windows | All walls on affected room complete |
| Interior partitions | Exterior walls complete |
| Dimensions | All geometry for that room complete |
| Furniture / blocks | Room layout complete |
| Annotations / text | Geometry + dimensions complete |

---

## Phase Sizing Rules

| Rule | Reason |
|------|--------|
| Maximum 20 tool calls per phase step | Limits damage from a failure |
| Maximum 7 steps per phase | Forces clear sub-goals |
| One quality gate per phase | Verification is non-negotiable |
| One checkpoint per phase | Recovery requires save points |
| One phase at a time | Never start Phase N+1 while Phase N is unverified |

---

## Execution Order

1. Drawing setup (create drawing, set INSUNITS, create layers)
2. Site or bounding geometry (site boundary, reference lines)
3. Primary structure (exterior walls, major structural elements)
4. Secondary structure (interior partitions, columns)
5. Openings (doors, windows — cut into walls)
6. Dimensions (annotate completed geometry)
7. Text and labels
8. Paper space / layout (if required)

This order cannot be reversed arbitrarily. You cannot add doors before the
walls exist. You cannot dimension geometry that doesn't exist.

---

## When to Plan vs. When to Execute

| Request Type | Agent Response |
|-------------|---------------|
| "Draw a line from A to B" | No phase planning — execute immediately (GREEN) |
| "Create a 6×4m room" | 1-step plan, confirm with user, execute |
| "Design a 2-bedroom apartment" | Full phase plan, present for approval, then execute Phase 1 |
| "Design a 5-floor building" | Full phase plan, stop after plan delivery, wait for requirements + approval |

---

## Re-planning Triggers

Re-plan (do not blindly continue) when:

- A phase fails its quality gate
- A prerequisite is found to be incomplete when the next phase begins
- The user modifies a requirement after planning is complete
- The agent detects a state mismatch in the DWG
- The user requests a change to an already-planned element

When re-planning, clearly state what changed and why the plan was updated.

---

## Plan Presentation Format

For MODERATE and above, present the plan before execution:

```
PROJECT PLAN: [Name]
Complexity: [level]
Phases: [N]

Phase 01 — [Name] (est. [N] tool calls)
  Goal: [single sentence]
  Risk: 🟢 GREEN
  
Phase 02 — [Name] (est. [N] tool calls)
  Goal: [single sentence]
  Risk: 🟡 YELLOW
  Requires approval before starting

Phase 03 — [Name] (est. [N] tool calls)
  Goal: [single sentence]  
  Risk: 🔴 RED — [why red]
  Requires explicit approval before starting

Checkpoints: After each phase
First phase to execute: Phase 01

→ Type "approve" to begin Phase 01.
→ Type "modify" to change the plan.
→ Type "stop" to save the plan without executing.
```

# Reference Lookup Rules

The agent may consult the local engineering reference library during
UNDERSTAND and PLAN. Retrieved passages are evidence with confidence
labels — never verdicts, never approvals, never geometric proof.

---

## Step 1 — Decide Whether to Search

Search when the request involves any of:

- A named code, standard, clearance, or minimum dimension the user did
  not fully specify ("per code", "standard door", "accessible clearance")
- A material, system, or sizing choice the user left open
- A claim of the form "standard X says Y" that needs a source

Do NOT search for pure geometry the user fully specified, and never
search instead of asking about project-specific unknowns (site
dimensions, placements, user preferences). If no library is configured,
skip this entire file and proceed exactly as before.

---

## Step 2 — Run the Search

Run the repository search command from the runtime environment with
explicit library roots, for example:

```text
python tools/ref_search.py --lib global=<global-root> --lib project=<project-root> --query "door clearance" --json
```

Pin `--ref` to one reference id when the discipline is known. Prefer
`--json` output for machine-readable hits. The command reads page
indexes only; it never opens PDF files and never transcribes scanned
pages. No OCR engine is installed or invoked anywhere in this workflow.

---

## Step 3 — Handle Failure by Degrading, Never by Inventing

If the library is absent, an index is missing, a source is
unavailable, or the answer is an explicit no-match: record the short
phrase "no reference evidence" and continue the existing workflow
unchanged. Reference failures MUST NOT block planning, corrupt project
state, or produce passages. A missing passage is information, not an
error to work around with a guessed value.

---

## Step 4 — Separate Excerpt from Interpretation

Every used passage keeps two strictly separated parts:

- **Excerpt (verbatim):** the retrieved text plus its reference id,
  page, method tag, confidence, and flags. Copy it exactly.
- **Interpretation (agent's own words):** what the agent concludes for
  this project, in a separate field or paragraph — never interleaved
  with the excerpt.

Repeat the method tag, confidence, and any flags every time a passage
is reused. Passages marked `low`, `unverified`, or carrying
`legacy-ocr-layer`, `encoding-suspect`, or partial-source flags are
presented with their limits spoken aloud. Missing page or section
evidence is reported as unverified with downgraded-lead wording.

---

## Step 5 — Respect the Prohibitions

- **No compliance verdicts.** Phrases like "complies with X" stay
  RED professional-judgment stops. A retrieved passage supports the
  engineer's decision; it never replaces it.
- **No dimensional verification from text.** Passages inform
  *requirements* (which value to use), never *measurements* (whether
  the drawing matches). Geometry evidence rules are unchanged.
- **No handbook as mandatory code.** When a compliance, load, safety,
  or dimension question is answered from a handbook, manufacturer, or
  educational source, label it as such every time: a handbook is not a
  substitute for the applicable mandatory code.
- **No silent upgrades.** Never raise a `low` passage to `high`
  without a spot-check against the original page. Never fill in a
  missing page number.

---

## Step 6 — Record Citations in Project Memory

Cited requirements store a citation object: reference id, page
(integer or null), method, confidence. See the `citation` fields in
the decision, assumption, and constraint schemas — all optional, all
backward-compatible. Uncited defaults stay assumptions with
confidence, exactly as before. A record claiming a source it cannot
show is a fabrication: omit the citation instead.

# Requirement Extraction Rules

When the user provides a design request, the agent must extract and structure
requirements before any planning or execution begins.

---

## Step 1 — Extract All Stated Requirements

Read the user's request carefully. Identify every stated element:

- Dimensions (width, height, area, clearance)
- Elements (rooms, doors, walls, columns)
- Relationships (adjacent to, connected by, north of)
- Materials or types (exterior wall, lightweight partition)
- Quantities (3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms)
- Performance criteria (minimum area, maximum span)

Write each requirement as:

```
REQ-NNN: [Element] [property] [value] [unit]
Source: [user / standard / regulation / default]
Priority: [HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW]
Verifiable: [Yes — how / No — why not]
```

`standard` and `regulation` sources come from the local library (see
`rules/reference_rules.md`) and carry a citation: reference id plus
page, method tag, and confidence. A requirement claiming a code or
standard without a citable passage stays an assumption, not a
requirement.

---

## Step 2 — Identify Missing Critical Requirements

A requirement is **critical** if its absence blocks the agent from planning
or executing correctly.

### Always required for ANY project:
- [ ] What type of project is this? (residential, commercial, structural...)
- [ ] What are the overall site or bounding dimensions?
- [ ] What units does the user expect? (mm, m, feet — agent works in mm internally)
- [ ] Is there an existing DWG to start from or is this a new drawing?

### Required for room/floor plan projects:
- [ ] Room dimensions (width × depth, or total area with shape)
- [ ] Wall thickness (exterior and interior) — if not stated, use standard defaults and RECORD THE ASSUMPTION
- [ ] Ceiling height — if not stated for 2D plan, record as assumption
- [ ] Door and window positions (if specific placement required)
- [ ] Which walls are load-bearing (if structural decisions are needed)

### Required for multi-floor projects:
- [ ] Number of floors
- [ ] Floor-to-floor height
- [ ] Vertical circulation (stairs, lifts)
- [ ] Structural system

---

## Step 3 — Identify Ambiguous Requirements

An ambiguous requirement has multiple valid interpretations that lead to
different designs.

| Signal | Ambiguity Type | Agent Response |
|--------|---------------|---------------|
| "normal", "standard", "typical" | Unquantified descriptor | Ask for specific dimension, or cite a retrieved passage as one option among explicitly asked choices (never as the decision) |
| "near", "close to", "adjacent" | Spatial relationship without dimension | Ask for clearance dimension |
| "a few", "some", "several" | Unquantified quantity | Ask for exact count |
| "large", "small", "comfortable" | Relative size | Ask for m² or mm |
| Location not specified | Positional ambiguity | Ask: "Where on [wall/floor]? Distance from [reference]?" |
| "with a door" without wall specification | Reference ambiguity | Ask: "Which wall? Distance from corner?" |

---

## Step 4 — Normalize Requirements

Convert all requirements to the agent's internal format:

| User Input | Normalized |
|-----------|-----------|
| "6 meters wide" | `width_mm: 6000` |
| "3 by 4" (context: metres) | `width_mm: 3000, depth_mm: 4000` |
| "900mm door" | `door_width_mm: 900` |
| "standard ceiling height" | `ceiling_height_mm: 2700` (assumption, record it) |
| "15 square meters" | `area_sqmm: 15000000, shape: TBD` |
| "south wall" | `wall: south — requires room boundary to be established first` |

---

## Step 5 — Completeness Check

Before beginning planning, all of the following must be true:

- [ ] Every HIGH-priority requirement has a specific, measurable value
- [ ] Every element that will be drawn has a target layer assigned
- [ ] Site/bounding dimensions are known
- [ ] No ambiguity exists in the position of the first element to be drawn
- [ ] All MEDIUM-priority requirements are either resolved or recorded as assumptions with confidence

If any HIGH-priority requirement is unresolved: **STOP and ask.**
If MEDIUM-priority items are unresolved: record as assumptions, continue.

---

## Step 6 — Present Requirements for Confirmation (Complex Projects Only)

For projects classified as MODERATE or above, present the extracted
requirements to the user before planning:

```
I have extracted the following requirements from your request:

Requirements:
  REQ-001: Room width = 6000mm (HIGH) ✓
  REQ-002: Room depth = 4000mm (HIGH) ✓
  REQ-003: Door on south wall, width = 900mm (HIGH) ✓

Assumptions I will use:
  ASM-001: Wall thickness = 200mm exterior, 100mm interior [MEDIUM confidence]
  ASM-002: Layer names: WALLS-EXT, WALLS-INT, DOORS [standard]

Evidence (when the local library was consulted):
  [REF-ID] p.[N] [method/confidence]: "[verbatim excerpt]"
  Interpretation: [what this means for the project, separate from the excerpt]
  Uncertainties: [limits, flags, or unverified locations, spoken plainly]

Missing (needs your input before I can begin):
  1. Where on the south wall should the door be placed?
     (distance from west corner, or centered?)

Do you confirm the requirements above and can you answer the missing item?
```

# Risk Classification Rules

Every planned operation must be classified before execution. The classification
determines whether the agent can proceed autonomously, must verify first, or
must request explicit human approval.

---

## 🟢 GREEN — Autonomous, No Prior Approval Needed

Proceed without requesting approval. Verify after execution.

### GREEN Operations

| Operation | MCP Tool(s) |
|-----------|------------|
| Check AutoCAD connection | `autocad_status` |
| Get drawing information | `get_active_drawing_info`, `list_open_drawings` |
| List drawing contents | `list_layers`, `list_blocks`, `list_layouts`, `query_entities` |
| Adjust view | `zoom_extents` |
| Take screenshot | `capture_screenshot` |
| Create a new layer | `create_layer` |
| Set current layer | `set_current_layer` |
| Modify layer properties | `set_layer_properties`, `set_layer_linetype` |
| Draw geometry in an **empty area** with no existing nearby entities | `draw_line`, `draw_circle`, `draw_arc`, `draw_ellipse`, `draw_polyline`, `draw_point` |
| Add text labels and annotations | `draw_text`, `draw_mtext` |
| Add measurement dimensions | `add_linear_dimension` |
| Copy an entity to an empty area | `copy_entity` |
| Change entity layer | `set_entity_layer` |
| Save the drawing | `save_active_drawing`, `save_drawing_as`, `save_drawing_explicit` |
| Create a new drawing | `create_new_drawing` |
| Open a drawing | `open_drawing` |

**GREEN post-execution:** Always run `query_entities` to confirm the entity
was created. Record the handle in the state file.

---

## 🟡 YELLOW — Proceed With Verification Before Continuing

Execute, then verify before proceeding to dependent steps. Do not start the
next phase until YELLOW operations are confirmed correct.

### YELLOW Operations

| Operation | Why Yellow | Required Verification |
|-----------|-----------|----------------------|
| Drawing a complete room layout | Composite of many elements; must form a closed, dimensionally correct space | Dimension all sides; verify entity count |
| Placing a door or window opening | Modifies wall boundary; affects circulation and clearance constraints | Dimension width; verify position on wall |
| Moving an entity | Changes relative positions; may affect dependent geometry | Dimension new position from reference; check constraints |
| Copying near existing geometry | Risk of overlap or duplicate | Inspect after; verify no overlap |
| Inserting a block | Block must exist; scale must be correct | Query entity; verify position |
| Any operation affecting 5–10 entities | Higher complexity, higher error risk | Full layer audit after |
| Batch creation of 5–10 entities | Multi-entity write in one call | Query the batch back before continuing |
| Dimensioning a finished phase | Must match requirements | Compare all measurements to requirements |
| Making an assumption about a dimension | Assumption must be recorded and flagged | Record in assumptions.md; flag as UNRESOLVED |

**YELLOW post-execution:** Run full verification before marking the phase step
complete. Record the assumption if the agent used a default value.

---

## 🔴 RED — Explicit Human Approval Required Before Execution

**Do not call any mutating MCP tool until the human has explicitly said "yes",
"approved", "proceed", or equivalent.**

### RED Operations

| Operation | Why Red | Approval Message Template |
|-----------|---------|--------------------------|
| `erase_entity` | Destructive; no programmatic undo | "I am about to erase [element] (handle: [H]). This cannot be undone programmatically. A checkpoint will be saved first. Approve?" |
| First execution of any plan phase | Irreversible changes to drawing begin | "I am ready to begin Phase [N]: [description]. This will modify the drawing. Approve?" |
| Any structural placement decision | Safety-critical; requires professional judgment | "I am about to place [element] which functions as [structural role]. This requires engineering approval. Please confirm this placement is correct." |
| Safety-critical dimensions | Egress, stair rise/run, fire ratings | "The [dimension] I am about to use is [value]. This is a life-safety dimension. Please confirm this value complies with your applicable building code." |
| Modifications affecting > 10 entities | High-impact operation | "This modification will affect [N] entities. A checkpoint will be saved. Please review the plan and approve." |
| Any operation the agent is uncertain about | Uncertainty is a stop condition | "I am not certain [X]. Before proceeding, I need you to confirm [Y]." |
| Major spatial reorganization | Risk of cascading constraint violations | "Reorganizing [element group] will affect [list of dependencies]. Please review the impact and approve." |
| Phase entry when plan was flagged for approval | Plan review point | "The plan designated Phase [N] as requiring approval before execution. Do you approve?" |

`draw_batch` follows this modification scale exactly — 1–4 items 🟢, 5–10 🟡, and **more than 10 🔴** — with no batch-specific exemption.

### erase_entity Exception (Temporary Verification Artifacts Only)

`erase_entity` remains **🔴 RED by default.** The ONE exception applies only
when **all** of the following are true:

1. The entity was created by the agent during the current verification operation;
2. The entity is a temporary verification artifact;
3. The entity is on the `_VERIFY_DIM` layer;
4. Removing it does not modify user-authored geometry.

When all four conditions hold, the erase may proceed as part of verification
cleanup without a separate RED approval request.

**This exception applies ONLY to temporary verification artifacts.**
Any erase of user-authored geometry remains 🔴 RED and requires explicit
human approval, regardless of circumstances.

### RED Approval Format

When requesting RED approval, always include:

```
🔴 APPROVAL REQUIRED

Operation: [what will happen]
Tool: [MCP tool name]
Affected elements: [list of elements]
Risk: [what can go wrong]
Checkpoint: [will save / has saved to path/to/checkpoint.dwg]
Reversibility: [how to recover if needed]

→ Type "approve" or "yes" to proceed.
→ Type "no" or "stop" to cancel.
→ Type "modify" to change the plan.
```

## Risk Escalation

The following conditions automatically escalate risk from YELLOW → RED:

1. The drawing has not been checkpointed in the last 5 phase steps
2. The operation involves a dimension flagged as safety-critical in `constraints.md`
3. An assumption involved in the operation is marked `UNRESOLVED` in `assumptions.md`
4. The agent detects a state mismatch (DWG differs from state record)
5. The user has manually modified the drawing (detected by entity count change)

# State Synchronization Rules

The agent's `project_state.md` represents what the agent BELIEVES is in the
drawing. The drawing is the ground truth. When they disagree, the drawing wins.

---

## The Stale State Problem

This scenario WILL happen:
1. Agent plans a modification (e.g. "Move door 500mm to the right").
2. User manually moves or edits the door in AutoCAD before the agent executes.
3. If the agent only checks entity count, the count has NOT changed!
4. The agent executes its old displacement vector, moving the door to an incorrect location.

Therefore, **entity counts alone are insufficient.** The current MCP exposes
no entity coordinates, so an entity's position cannot be numerically measured
independently. Before modifying, the agent must gather every available piece
of evidence — handle existence, layer/type/count checks, and screenshot
inspection — and must **STOP whenever that evidence cannot confirm the
expected state.**

---

## Pre-Session Sync Check (Always)

At the start of any `CONTINUE_PROJECT`, `MODIFY_PROJECT`, or `VERIFY_PROJECT` session:

```
Step 1: autocad_status → confirm AutoCAD connected
Step 2: get_active_drawing_info
  → Compare returned path to project_state.md "DWG Path"
  → If MISMATCH → STOP: wrong drawing is open

Step 3: For each layer listed in "State Sync Record" of project_state.md:
  query_entities (layer: [name], limit: 1000, max_scan: 5000)
  → Compare actual count to expected count in state
  → Record: MATCH or MISMATCH
  → If truncated == true: snapshot is incomplete — obtain a complete
    snapshot before trusting the result

Step 4: Validate handles in Handle Registry:
  Compare ALL expected handles that can be queried against the returned
  entities — not just a sample.
  → If truncated == true: do not draw a definitive conclusion; re-query
  → Any required handle missing → treat as stale state

Step 5: Verdict:
  → All layers MATCH + all handles OK → STATE IS FRESH → proceed
  → Layer count within ±1 + handles OK → MINOR DRIFT → warn + proceed carefully
  → Layer count off by >1 → SIGNIFICANT DRIFT → stop and re-inspect
  → Any target handle missing → HANDLE STALE → stop and re-inspect
  → Snapshot truncated / state cannot be trusted → STOP and re-analyze
```

---

## Pre-Execution Datum Check (Before Modifying Existing Geometry)

Before calling any mutating tool on existing entities (`move_entity`, `erase_entity`, etc.):

```
1. Identify the target entity by handle from the Handle Registry.
2. Existence check (primary evidence):
   query_entities (layer: [expected layer], limit: 1000, max_scan: 5000)
   - Confirm the handle is present in the results; truncated == false.
   - Handle missing → stale state → STOP.
   - Truncated snapshot → state cannot be trusted → STOP and re-query.

3. Layer / count check:
   - Compare entity counts against the State Sync Record.
   - Mismatch beyond tolerance → STOP and re-inspect.

4. Visual check:
   - zoom_extents () + capture_screenshot (width_px: 1400)
   - Confirm the drawing visually matches the expected state.

5. OPTIONAL measurement sanity check (NOT positional proof):
   - add_linear_dimension between agent-supplied points around the expected
     location on layer "_VERIFY_DIM"; read measurement_mm; erase the temp
     dimension (agent-created _VERIFY_DIM artifact — exception applies).
   - A MATCH confirms units/measurement behavior only — it does NOT prove
     the entity sits at that position (the MCP exposes no coordinates).
   - A MISMATCH is a failure signal → STOP.

6. Evaluate Datum Check:
   - Evidence (handle + counts + screenshot) consistent with project_state.md:
     → Safe to proceed with the planned displacement vector.
   - Evidence missing, inconsistent, or snapshot truncated:
     → STALE STATE CANNOT BE RULED OUT. The current MCP cannot numerically
       confirm an entity's position, so absence of proof is not proof.
     → DO NOT apply the planned displacement vector.
     → STOP immediately:
       "Stale state cannot be ruled out: [Element] expected [evidence], but
        [what was found]. The current MCP cannot independently measure entity
        position. Halting planned modification to prevent misplacement.
        Re-analyzing..."
```

---

## State Reconstruction (When State File is Missing)

If `project_state.md` does not exist for an existing drawing:

```
1. get_active_drawing_info → get name, path, INSUNITS
2. list_layers → inspect layer names and properties
3. query_entities on each layer → count and types
4. zoom_extents
5. capture_screenshot (verify was_foreground == true) → visual overview
6. Reconstruct a new project_state.md marked as [RECONSTRUCTED]
7. Present reconstruction to user and confirm before modifying anything.
```

---

## State Commit Policy (Avoiding Excessive File Writes)

To prevent context saturation and excessive file writes:
1. **During step-by-step execution:** Maintain new entity handles and progress in working memory.
2. **Before major mutations:** Save a checkpoint DWG via `save_drawing_as` and commit pre-change state.
3. **At sub-phase / phase completion:** Write the full updated `project_state.md`, `decisions.md`, and `change_log.md`.
4. **After verification:** Commit final verification results.

# Stop Conditions

The Engineering CAD Agent MUST stop execution and explain itself clearly
whenever any of the following conditions are true. Stopping is not a failure —
it is the correct engineering response to uncertainty or risk.

---

## Category A — Missing Requirements

Stop when a required value is not known and guessing would be wrong:

| Condition | Why it matters |
|-----------|---------------|
| A critical dimension is unspecified (e.g., wall height for a multi-floor building) | Wrong value propagates through all dependent phases |
| A room function is undefined but affects adjacency requirements | Placement decisions will be wrong |
| The structural system is unknown for a structural project | Cannot determine load paths |
| The project site dimensions are unknown | Cannot place anything |
| Building code jurisdiction is unknown for code-critical dimensions | Cannot validate egress, clearances |

**Action:** List every missing requirement. Ask specific, numbered questions.
Do not attempt to infer critical values from vague descriptions.

---

## Category B — Ambiguity Requiring Human Decision

Stop when two or more interpretations are valid and the choice affects design:

| Condition | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| Location of an element is underspecified | "Add a door to the wall" — which wall? where on the wall? |
| Dimension has an implicit range with multiple valid values | "A normal-sized bedroom" — 10m²? 12m²? 15m²? |
| Conflicting requirements exist | REQ-001 says kitchen north, REQ-004 says kitchen adjacent to south entrance |
| User says "standard" without specifying which standard | "Standard ceiling height" — which building code? |

**Action:** Present the ambiguity explicitly. Offer specific options where possible.
Wait for the user to choose before proceeding.

---

## Category C — Verification Failure

Stop when the agent cannot confirm the work is correct:

| Condition | Trigger |
|-----------|---------|
| A measurement sanity check does not match the required dimension | `measurement_mm` from `add_linear_dimension` ≠ expected value (a mismatch is a failure signal; a match proves only the measurement, not entity geometry) |
| Correction has been attempted 2 times and still fails | Repeated verification failure |
| An expected entity cannot be found in `query_entities` | Entity creation may have silently failed |
| A critical quality gate fails and the next phase depends on it | Cannot continue to dependent work on a broken foundation |

**Action:** Report the exact discrepancy. Explain what was expected vs. what was
found. List options for recovery. Do not attempt a third correction autonomously.

---

## Category D — State Inconsistency

Stop when the DWG state does not match what the agent expects:

| Condition | Trigger |
|-----------|---------|
| A handle from `project_state.md` is not returned by `query_entities` on its expected layer | User may have manually deleted or modified the entity |
| State evidence (handles / counts / screenshot) cannot confirm the expected entity state before a modification | Position cannot be numerically measured with the current MCP; applying a stale displacement would cause misplacement |
| Entity count on a layer differs significantly from the state record | User may have modified the drawing manually |
| `get_active_drawing_info` returns a different file path than expected | Wrong drawing is open |
| `unit_warning` is present and measurements are being relied upon | Unitless drawing — measurements are unreliable |
| The drawing is read-only (`readonly: true`) | Cannot write to this drawing |

**Action:** Describe what was expected vs. what was found. Offer to re-inspect
the DWG and rebuild the state record. Do not proceed with stale assumptions.

---

## Category E — Risk and Approval

Stop when explicit human approval has not been given for a risky operation:

| Condition | Risk Level |
|-----------|-----------|
| About to call `erase_entity` on any entity **except agent-created temporary verification artifacts on `_VERIFY_DIM`** (see `risk_rules.md` erase exception) | 🔴 RED |
| About to make a structural placement decision | 🔴 RED |
| About to modify safety-critical dimensions (egress, stair geometry) | 🔴 RED |
| About to execute the first phase of a plan that has not been reviewed | 🔴 RED |
| About to modify 10+ entities in a single operation | 🔴 RED |
| Entering a phase that was flagged for approval in the plan | 🔴 RED |

**Action:** Present the operation, describe what it will do, identify what it
will affect, and ask: "Do you approve this operation? [Yes / No / Modify the plan]"

---

## Category F — AutoCAD Connection Problems

Stop when the tool layer is unavailable:

| Condition | Response |
|-----------|----------|
| `autocad_status` returns `ok: false` | Stop all operations. Inform user AutoCAD is not connected. |
| A tool call fails with a connection error (e.g. `"No running AutoCAD session was found..."` or `"AutoCAD COM error: ..."`) | Stop. AutoCAD may have crashed or been closed. |
| COM error on geometry tool | Stop the current operation. Do not retry blindly. Inspect state first. |
| No active drawing | Inform user to open or create a drawing in AutoCAD. |

---

## Category G — Engineering Judgment Required

Stop when the decision requires professional engineering knowledge:

| Condition | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| Load-bearing determination | "Is this wall structural?" |
| Foundation type selection | "What foundation does this building need?" |
| MEP routing decisions | "Where should the HVAC ducts run?" |
| Fire compartment boundaries | "Which walls need to be fire-rated?" |
| Seismic or wind design | "What is the required wall bracing?" |

**Action:** Clearly state that this decision requires professional engineering
judgment. The agent can model what the engineer decides, but cannot make
structural or safety decisions autonomously.

---

## Category H — Complexity Overload

Stop when the request is too large for single-cycle execution:

| Condition | Threshold |
|-----------|-----------|
| Project has > 5 identifiable phases | Decompose and plan first; do not execute |
| Phase has > 20 individual tool calls | Split the phase |
| A single modification affects > 10 entities | Plan and get approval before executing |
| The request is for an entire building with no requirements | Gather requirements first |

---

## How to Stop Correctly

When stopping, always provide:

```
STOP REASON: [Category and specific condition]

WHAT WAS EXPECTED: [what the agent planned to do]

WHAT WAS FOUND / WHAT IS MISSING: [the specific problem]

WHAT IS NEEDED TO CONTINUE:
  1. [specific answer or action required]
  2. [specific answer or action required]

CURRENT STATE: [safe — no changes made / partial — changes saved at checkpoint]
```

Never stop silently. Never stop with just "I can't do that."

# Verification Rules

The agent verifies all work. A tool returning `ok: true` is **not** verification.
Verification requires independently observing or checking the result — by
screenshot inspection, handle/existence queries, layer/type/count checks, and
(where available) measurement sanity checks.

---

## Core Principle

> "A successful tool call proves that the API accepted the command.
> It does NOT prove that the correct geometry exists at the correct position
> with the correct dimensions."

The agent must always close the loop:
**Execute → Observe → Compare → Pass or Fail**

---

## What the Current MCP Can and Cannot Verify (MVP)

The MCP server does NOT expose entity coordinates/vertices. No tool returns
line endpoints, polyline vertices, or entity centers. This bounds what
verification can honestly claim.

### Verified reliably (primary evidence for MVP)

| Evidence | MCP Tool |
|----------|----------|
| Entity existence / handle creation | `query_entities` (handle appears in results) |
| Object type | `query_entities` (`object_name`) |
| Layer assignment | `query_entities` (`layer`) |
| Entity counts | `query_entities` (`total_in_space`, count vs. State Sync Record) |
| Operation response | tool response `ok: true` |
| Save result | `get_active_drawing_info` (`saved: true`) |
| Screenshot evidence | `capture_screenshot` (inspect returned image) |
| Visual alignment when observable in the screenshot | screenshot inspection |

**MVP primary verification = handle/existence checks + layer/type checks +
screenshot inspection + operation result.**

### NOT numerically verifiable with the current MCP

- Actual line endpoints
- Actual polyline vertices
- Actual entity center
- Actual entity position
- Actual entity length independent of supplied measurement points

`add_linear_dimension` measures between **agent-supplied points**. A dimension
whose `measurement_mm` matches an expectation therefore does **NOT** constitute
independent proof of the drawn entity's geometry — if the entity were drawn
elsewhere, the same points would still produce the same measurement.

---

## Verification Toolkit (MCP-Based)

These are the tools available for verification. Use exact signatures from `tool_contracts.md`.

| Verification Need | Role | MCP Tool | How to Use |
|------------------|------|----------|-----------|
| Entity was created | **Primary** | `query_entities` | Filter by `layer` + `object_name`; confirm new handle in diff |
| Element on correct layer | **Primary** | `query_entities` | Filter by expected layer; handle should appear in result |
| No duplicates | **Primary** | `query_entities` | Compare handles against pre-operation snapshot (`limit: 1000`, `max_scan: 5000`, `truncated == false`) |
| Entity type / counts | **Primary** | `query_entities` | `object_name` + count vs. state record |
| Spatial layout / visual alignment | **Primary** | `zoom_extents` + `capture_screenshot` | Visual review of MCP returned image; confirm `was_foreground == true` |
| Drawing is saved | **Primary** | `get_active_drawing_info` | Check `saved: true` after `save_active_drawing` |
| Line length / room width (unit sanity) | **Sanity check only** | `add_linear_dimension` | Dimension between supplied points; read `measurement_mm` — confirms units/measurement behavior, **not** the entity's actual geometry |

---

## Dimensional Checks Are Sanity Checks, Not Geometry Proof

The dimensional operation (`add_linear_dimension`) may still be used as a
**unit / AutoCAD measurement sanity check**, but the Skill must never describe
it as independent geometry verification:

- ✓ Acceptable: "measurement between [0,0] and [6000,0] returned 6000mm —
  unit conversion behaves as expected."
- ✗ Not acceptable: "the north wall is at y=4000 because the dimension
  returned 4000mm." The dimension measured the supplied points, not the wall.

When a sanity check disagrees with expectations, treat it as a failure signal
and STOP (a mismatch still indicates a problem). When it agrees, it confirms
only the measurement, not the entity position.

**Record all verification dimensions.** Erase them only after confirming the
measurement. Do NOT erase a dimension before reading it. Cleanup of
agent-created `_VERIFY_DIM` artifacts falls under the verification-artifact
exception in `risk_rules.md` (no separate RED approval; all four conditions
must hold).

---

## Phase Quality Gate Procedure

Run this at the end of every phase before updating `project_state.md` as COMPLETE:

```
1. zoom_extents
   → Ensures all geometry is visible in active window

2. capture_screenshot (width_px: 1400)
   → Inspect returned image content in MCP response
   → Verify data["was_foreground"] == true
   → This screenshot is PRIMARY verification evidence

3. For each HIGH-priority dimension in this phase (SANITY CHECK — not
   independent geometry verification):
   add_linear_dimension
     start_mm: [reference point]
     end_mm: [element endpoint]
     dimension_line_point_mm: [offset from line]
     orientation: "aligned" (or "horizontal" / "vertical")
     layer: "_VERIFY_DIM"
   → Read measurement_mm from response data
   → Compare to requirement: |measurement_mm - required_mm| ≤ 1mm → PASS
   → If difference > 1mm → FAIL
   → NOTE: measurement_mm is computed from the supplied points; a match
     confirms units/measurement behavior only, NOT the entity's geometry.

4. erase_entity (handle: [dimension handle])
   → Clean up temporary verification dimension
   → Agent-created artifact on _VERIFY_DIM — verification-artifact exception
     in risk_rules.md applies (all four conditions must hold)

5. query_entities (layer: "[phase layer]", limit: 1000, max_scan: 5000)
   → Confirm all expected handles are present; truncated == false

6. Evaluate constraint checklist (from constraints.md):
   → Each constraint applicable to this phase: PASS or FAIL
   → Constraints involving actual entity position can be confirmed
     visually in the screenshot only (MCP exposes no coordinates)

7. Quality gate verdict (based on primary evidence):
   → Expected handles present & correct type/layer ✓
   → Screenshot visually acceptable & foreground ✓
   → Entity counts match state ✓
   → All applicable constraints: PASS ✓
   → Sanity-check dimensions: PASS ✓
   → → PHASE QUALITY GATE: PASS

   → Any FAIL → PHASE QUALITY GATE: FAIL → do not proceed
```

## Correction Procedure (When Quality Gate Fails)

```
Attempt 1:
  1. Diagnose: which specific check failed? what value was found vs. expected?
  2. Form a correction plan: what tool call(s) will fix this?
  3. If fix requires erasing → checkpoint first via save_drawing_as
  4. Execute correction
  5. Re-run quality gate

Attempt 2 (if Attempt 1 fails):
  1. Capture screenshot to review current visual state
  2. Try an alternative correction approach
  3. Execute
  4. Re-run quality gate

If both attempts fail:
  STOP — BLOCKED
  Report: what was attempted, what was found each time, what is needed
  Do NOT continue to the next phase
  Do NOT attempt a third autonomous correction
```
